evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: Practice: pregnant women enrolled at four rural health centers in Mchinji district, Malawi, take one iron-folate tablet every day from the first antenatal visit. We interviewed 28 pregnant women alone. Most said the tablets are good for the baby, yet many stop. When we asked whose opinion matters, they named the husband and his mother; most said they would take the tablets if those two told them to, and most believe those two are against 'hospital medicine' in pregnancy. Several also said they watch what other pregnant women in the village do. Respondents: about 600 pregnant women aged 18 to 40 at antenatal visits, most with primary schooling, each interviewed alone in a private room, in Chichewa, by a female surveyor who reads the questions aloud. Taking the tablets is not illegal or shameful here. Please write the vignette for our baseline survey.
evals.expected_output: A norms vignette in the output template with one base story, four versions that differ only in the two cues, and a stated reading of the answers.
assertions: The base story is about a named fictional pregnant woman like the respondents and is not set in the respondents' own village.
The empirical cue names pregnant women in her village and the normative cue names her husband and his mother; neither says 'people'.
Gives four versions that differ only in the cue sentences, assigned at random, one per respondent.
Asks what the fictional woman will do and whether the respondent thinks she should.
Says in advance what a shift with each cue, or with neither, would mean.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Write a norms vignette about saving.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the practice, whose behavior and approval people track, and the respondents, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks who does what, when, or for the evidence that others' expectations matter.
Asks whose behavior and whose approval people track for this practice.
Asks who the respondents are or how the survey is delivered.
Does not write a story or cues.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We want vignettes on girls marrying before 18 in rural Amhara, Ethiopia. Our interviews with parents suggest families marry daughters early because the extended family and the church elders expect it. Respondents will be girls aged 13 to 17 and their parents, interviewed at home in Amharic by surveyors reading aloud. Can you write the four versions?
evals.expected_output: The skill gives the design in outline and withholds the wording until a local qualitative researcher and an ethics reviewer have seen it.
assertions: Does not write the final wording of the story or the cues.
Gives the design in outline: the two cues with the reference group named, four versions, and the questions.
Names a local qualitative researcher who knows the practice and an ethics reviewer.
Gives a reason tied to this case: respondents who are minors, interviews at home within hearing of the family, or a version in which elders approve of early marriage.
Says what to bring to them.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: In our antenatal program in Malawi we want to know what share of women secretly stop taking the iron-folate tablets their clinic gives them. Can a vignette measure that?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the question is how common the respondents' own hidden behavior is and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says a vignette measures what respondents expect of others, not how many of them do something.
